questions.question: Which interface is the root for List, Set and Queue in the Collection Framework?
questions.explanation: List, Set and Queue all extend Collection, which itself extends Iterable. Map has a separate hierarchy.

questions.question: Why does Map not extend the Collection interface?
options: A map stores key-value pairs, so single-item methods like add(item) do not fit
Map cannot be iterated at all
Map is a class, not an interface
questions.explanation: Collection methods work on single items. A map works on pairs, but it offers keySet(), values() and entrySet() views.

questions.question: What does this print? Set<String> s = new HashSet<>(); s.add("A"); s.add("A"); System.out.println(s.size());
questions.explanation: A Set keeps only unique items. The second add returns false and the size stays 1.

questions.question: What does this print? Queue<String> q = new ArrayDeque<>(); q.offer("X"); q.offer("Y"); System.out.println(q.poll() + q.peek());
questions.explanation: poll removes and returns the head X. Then peek looks at the new head Y without removing it.

questions.question: Why does this line not compile? Collection<String> c = new HashMap<>();
options: The diamond <> is not allowed here
HashMap must be imported from java.lang
questions.explanation: HashMap implements Map, which is not a Collection. Use Map<K, V> as the variable type instead.

questions.question: You need unique member IDs that always come out in sorted order. Which class fits?
questions.explanation: TreeSet rejects duplicates and keeps items sorted. HashSet also rejects duplicates but gives no order.

questions.question: List<Integer> view = Collections.unmodifiableList(days); view.add(3); What happens?
options: 3 is added to days as well
questions.explanation: The unmodifiable view blocks every change through it and throws UnsupportedOperationException on add.

questions.question: What is the difference between Collection and Collections?
options: They are two names for the same interface
Collection is a class and Collections is an interface
Collections is the thread-safe version of Collection
Collection is an interface; Collections is a helper class of static methods
questions.explanation: You store data in a Collection. Collections offers static helpers such as sort, max, frequency and unmodifiableList.

questions.question: What does this print? Set<String> t = new TreeSet<>(Arrays.asList("C", "A", "B")); System.out.println(t);
questions.explanation: TreeSet stores its items in sorted order, so the strings print alphabetically whatever order they were added in.

questions.question: Which interface lets every collection be used in a for-each loop?
questions.explanation: Iterable provides iterator(), and the for-each loop calls it behind the scenes. Collection extends Iterable.
